:::{#exr-epe-three-sources}
#### Expected squared error from three sources

A prediction $g\paren{x; \trainset}$ at a covariate value $x$ has
squared bias $[\bias{g\paren{x; \trainset}}]^2 = 1$
and variance $\Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}} = 2$.
The new outcome is $Y_0 = \mean(x) + \noise$,
where $\noise$ has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar = 3$
and is independent of $g\paren{x; \trainset}$.

1. What is the expected squared prediction error $\E{(Y_0 - g\paren{x; \trainset})^2}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $g\paren{x; \trainset}$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (squared bias, variance of $g\paren{x; \trainset}$, $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
